Interval arithmetic gives definite and possible qualification and bounds $Y_L,Y_U$ for each of $E^*$, $T^*$ and $30|T^*-E^*|$. Let $r_{\rm def},r_{\rm poss}$ be their empirical qualification shares and let $\widehat G_{\rm def,U}(x)$ and $\widehat G_{\rm poss,L}(x)$ be the corresponding empirical subdistribution functions, normalized by the full supported station count $n$. Twenty empirical-process events across both boundaries receive failure probability $\alpha/20$, with $\alpha=0.05$ and $\varepsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(40/\alpha)/(2n)}$ \citep{Hoeffding1963,Reeve2024}. The conditional distribution is bounded by
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_-&=[r_{\rm def}-\varepsilon_n-\delta]_+,&
p_+&=\min\{1,r_{\rm poss}+\varepsilon_n+\delta\},\\
L(x)&=\frac{[\widehat G_{\rm def,U}(x)-\varepsilon_n-\delta]_+}{p_+},&
U(x)&=\min\left\{1,\frac{\widehat G_{\rm poss,L}(x)+\varepsilon_n+\delta}{p_-}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Positive denominators permit inversion to quantile bounds. A zero lower denominator gives an unbounded set. Bounds for joint qualification and deterministic interval transformations yield simultaneous coverage of the three targets under the stated assumptions. The $\delta$ term allows endpoint-box errors in population probabilities. $\alpha$ controls the empirical-process event.
